A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with reliably corresponding main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendix A. Lower-resolution versions of two figures in v3 do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.2-4.3 report original motion-decoding and brain-encoding results for three participants. Appendix A includes reconstruction examples and empirical controls.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and appendix results, and adds quantitative video-generation results in Table 1.

M1.justification: The fMRI/DINOv2 optical-flow classifier, FlowSAM masking, DragNUWA animation and ridge-regression encoding are retained. BrainNRDS is a new name; the added architecture paragraph documents the decoder without establishing a change to its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Dynamic Natural Vision dataset, three participants, decoding and encoding tasks, and reconstruction scenarios. Appendix A.4 retains the same pretraining-dataset controls. Table 1 evaluates existing reconstruction coverage.

E2.justification: MindVideo and Stable Video Diffusion remain the motion baselines, and the encoding/control comparator sets are unchanged. Table 1 adds metrics against the already evaluated MindVideo; NeuroClips receives discussion but no reported evaluation.

E3.justification: v3 adds video-generation evaluation using cosine similarity between averaged VideoMAE features, corresponding-frame CLIP cosine similarity, and SSIM (Table 1; Section 4.2). The existing flow and encoding protocols, data splits and preprocessing remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The action/camera-motion case studies and controls for model size, pretraining-data size and dataset distribution are retained unchanged (Figure 4, Figures S4-S5 and Tables S1-S2). No new ablation or robustness test is reported.

E5.justification: Table 1 introduces two-sample t-tests for video-generation comparisons, reporting p < 0.05. Existing SEM plots and paired/one-sample tests remain. The new table includes undefined ± quantities; the PDFs do not establish additional repeated runs.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports end-to-end versus MindVideo scores of 0.769 versus 0.742 for VideoMAE cosine similarity, 0.896 versus 0.879 for CLIP cosine similarity, and 0.214 versus 0.171 for SSIM, plus subject-specific results. Existing flow, encoding and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same fMRI, video and optical-flow definitions and classifier mapping. Neither version contains formal propositions or proofs; v3 adds no mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The four headline contributions remain unchanged, but v3 drops the conclusion’s prospective claim about helping construct better brain-machine interfaces. This slightly narrows the stated impact.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive contrast between optical flow’s explicit motion magnitude/direction and NeuroClips’ blurred-video proxy, and explains temporal consistency through motion-conditioned diffusion. The dataset-generalization and subject-specific training limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly describes the decoder’s MLP, spatial broadcasting, residual 1x1 convolutions, dropout and pooling. Conversely, v3 removes the Titan RTX, memory and up-to-12-hour training disclosure. It also replaces the example-website address.

R1.justification: v3 expands the comparison with the already-cited NeuroClips, distinguishing blurred-video and optical-flow representations. It removes the Yamins and DiCarlo (2016) reference; the other cited works are retained after renumbering.

P1.justification: v3 introduces BrainNRDS terminology throughout, shortens introductory examples and captions, tightens methodological prose, and updates author/contact presentation. The main section sequence and Appendix A organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 1, relocates several existing figures and compacts the author and supplement headings. Existing figures retain their scientific content, but Figures 6 and S1 are substantially downsampled, visibly reducing image detail and brain-region label clarity.

improvement.justification: Table 1 adds quantitative semantic and structural evaluation to reconstruction evidence previously centered on flow error and examples. Together with the decoder architecture description, this modestly strengthens evidence and transparency. These gains outweigh the limited losses from removed hardware/runtime information and blurrier Figures 6 and S1, although Table 1’s uncertainty statistic remains undefined.
